@graph.name: Elenchon Atlas — WPS Review & Approval Software
@graph.description: Cloud WPS review-and-approval software: every import queues as a change-set showing current value beside new value, cell by cell, with low-confidence reads flagged, drift detection between library and register, a configurable approval bar, and only approved cells patched into your own workbook.
@graph.keywords: WPS review software, WPS approval workflow, WPS change management, human-reviewed register edits, WPS register control, WPS drift detection
featureList: Cell-by-cell change-set showing current value versus new value
Inline correction and add-a-row before approval
Low-confidence and computed reads flagged in amber
Configurable approval bar: review all, review uncertain only, or auto-apply
Drift detection between library documents and the register with reviewed re-sync
Only approved cells patched into your own workbook; every change-set versioned

mainEntity.name: Does an import change my register automatically?
A big import has hundreds of cells. Do I have to check every one?
Can I correct a value during review?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fix any value inline, or add a row for a field the parser missed, then approve. What lands is what you signed off on — you're never forced to accept the parser's raw read or reject the whole set.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a WPS changes after its values landed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drift detection catches it: the app tells you the register is out of sync with the library and offers to re-sync the affected rows as a fresh change-set, reviewed and approved like any other — the sheet never quietly drifts from the documents behind it.

mainEntity.name: Does it rebuild my whole spreadsheet?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Atlas patches only the approved cells into your own workbook and leaves everything else exactly as you had it. Your file is never regenerated from a model, and every approved change-set is versioned so you can roll back.

mainEntity.name: What if an import has nothing to change, only something to verify?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's closed with a "mark reviewed" rather than an approval that would write an identical new version — so a verification-only change-set doesn't leave you stuck between approving a change that isn't there and rejecting a correct read.
